Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

LONDON, England (CNN) -- Kimi Raikkonen has lambasted McLaren's Lewis Hamilton for the pit-lane accident that ended both of their races at the Canadian Grand Prix. Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen is far from happy after Lewis Hamilton  pushed him out of the Canadian Grand Prix. Hamilton's McLaren rammed into the back of world champion Raikkonen's Ferrari as the Finn and Robert Kubica, the race's eventual winner, were waiting at a red light after the safety car was forced into action on lap 17. Raikkonen, while claiming not to be angry, was clearly far from impressed. "There's not much I can say. My race was ruined by Hamilton's mistake. "Obviously, anyone can make mistakes, as I did two weeks ago in Monaco, but it's one thing to make a mistake at 200 hundred [miles] per hour but another to hit a car stopped at a red light. "I'm not angry because that doesn't achieve anything and does not change my result. I am unhappy because I had a great chance of winning." Raikkonen, who has failed to score points in the previous two races, said he had to start winning again. "There is still a long way to go in the championship and it is still very close and we have everything we need to regain the ground we have lost." Ferrari team sporting director Stefano Domenicali said Hamilton had made a "serious mistake." "I think the penalty imposed by the FIA [Hamilton was given a 10-place grid penalty for the French Grand Prix at Magny-Cours] is in line with it, even if it does not restore what was a lost opportunity for us. "Kimi was in an excellent position to fight for the win" Hamilton, for his part, was apologetic. "I don't know what happened to be honest," Hamilton said. "I was comfortably in the lead, it was looking like an easy win. Then I went in for the pit stop. It was not a good stop and I saw the two guys in front of me battling in the pit lane. "I saw the red light but by that time it was a bit late. It was not exactly a racing incident as such, it was unfortunate. It was one of those things. It is different to if you crash into the wall and you are angry. It is not like that. I apologize to Kimi for ruining his race."

Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen was left deeply frustrated after Lewis Hamilton forced him out of contention at the event.

Hamilton's McLaren collided with the rear of world champion Raikkonen's Ferrari as the Finn, alongside Robert Kubica—the race's eventual winner—waited at a red light following the deployment of the safety car on lap 17.

Raikkonen, while insisting he was not angry, made no attempt to conceal his displeasure. "There's not much I can say. My race was ruined by Hamilton's mistake," he remarked.

"Obviously, anyone can make mistakes, as I did two weeks ago in Monaco. But it's one thing to make a mistake at 200 miles per hour, and quite another to hit a car stopped at a red light.

"I'm not angry, because that achieves nothing and does not change my result. I am simply unhappy, because I had a great chance of winning."

Raikkonen, who had failed to score points in the previous two races, stressed that he needed to return to winning ways. "There is still a long way to go in the championship, and it remains very close. We have everything we need to recover the ground we have lost."

Ferrari's sporting director, Stefano Domenicali, described Hamilton's actions as a "serious mistake."

"I believe the penalty imposed by the FIA—Hamilton was handed a 10-place grid penalty for the French Grand Prix at Magny-Cours—is in line with the offense, even if it does not restore what was a lost opportunity for us.

"Kimi was in an excellent position to fight for the win."

Hamilton, for his part, was contrite. "To be honest, I don't know what happened," he admitted. "I was comfortably in the lead, and it was looking like an easy victory. Then I came in for my pit stop. It was not a good stop, and I saw the two drivers ahead of me battling in the pit lane.

"I saw the red light, but by then it was a little too late. It was not exactly a racing incident as such—it was simply unfortunate, one of those things. It is different from crashing into a wall, where you feel angry. It's not like that. I apologize to Kimi for ruining his race."

He added: "I spotted the red light, but by then it was too late. This wasn't really a typical racing incident—it was just bad luck, one of those situations. It's not the same as crashing into a wall and being furious. That's not how it feels. I apologize to Kimi for spoiling his race."

The crash occurred as the field responded to a safety car period. "I was stopped at the red light, which is where you're supposed to stop," Raikkonen said. "There was nothing I could do. I was just sitting there waiting for the light and suddenly I got hit from behind. It's not a nice way to end the race when you haven't done anything wrong."

"I feel terrible about it. Kimi did nothing wrong — he was stopped exactly where he should have been. I misjudged the braking and there was nothing I could do to avoid it by the time I realised. I can only say sorry and learn from it."
